L196: # MS-SWIFT
L197: 
L198: ModelScope SWIFT (ms-swift) is the large model and multimodal large model training and deployment framework provided by the cite75†ModelScope community†modelscope.cn .
L199: 
L200: GitHub repository: cite76†ms-swift L201: 
L202: Features of using ms-swift for training LLM:
L203:   * Model Types: Supports 500+ plain-text large models and 200+ multimodal large models, covering the entire process from training to deployment.
L204:   * Hardware Support: Compatible with CPUs, RTX series GPUs, T4/V100, A10/A100/H100, Ascend NPUs, MPS, and more.
L205:   * Training Methods: Supports full-parameter fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA, and other techniques.
L206:   * Distributed Training: Supports distributed training technologies such as DDP, device_map, DeepSpeed ZeRO-2/ZeRO-3, FSDP, and integrates parallelism techniques from Megatron, including Tensor Parallelism, Pipeline Parallelism, Sequence Parallelism, and Expert Parallelism.
L207:   * RLHF Training: Supports human alignment methods like DPO, GRPO, DAPO, RM, PPO, KTO, etc., for both plain-text and multimodal large models.
L208: This article will demonstrate runnable training demos and provide the format for custom datasets. It includes how to use ms-swift for SFT and GRPO on Qwen3-8B, as well as using Megatron-SWIFT (ms-swift's integration of Megatron-LM) for SFT on Qwen3-30B-A3B. Through expert parallelism technology, MoE model training can be accelerated by nearly 10 times.
L209: Before starting fine-tuning, ensure your environment is properly set up.
L210: 
L211:     pip install ms-swift -U
L212:     # Install from source
L213:     pip install git+https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift.git
L214: 
L215:     pip install transformers -U
L216: 
L217:     # Optional packages
L218:     pip install deepspeed # multi-GPU training
L219:     pip install liger-kernel # save GPU memory resources
L220:     pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation
L221: ## Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
L222: ### Data Preparation
L223: 
L224: The custom dataset format for SFT using ms-swift is as follows (the system field is optional). You can organize it into formats such as JSON, JSONL, or CSV. Specify `--dataset <dataset_path>` in the training script.
L225: 
L226: For complete dataset formatting guidelines, see: cite77†Custom Dataset Documentation†swift.readthedocs.io L227:   * General format
L228: 
L229:     {"messages": [
L230:         {"role": "system", "content": "<system-prompt>"},
L231:         {"role": "user", "content": "<query1>"},
L232:         {"role": "assistant", "content": "<response1>"}
L233:     ]}
L234: 
L235:   * Format with think
L236: 
L237:     {"messages": [
L238:         {"role": "user", "content": "Where is the capital of Zhejiang?"},
L239:         {"role": "assistant", "content": "<think>\n...\n</think>\n\n The capital of Zhejiang is Hangzhou."}
L240:     ]}
L241: If you want to train using data without a chain of thought but retain the model's reasoning ability, there are two approaches to minimize disruption during fine-tuning:
L242: Option 1: During training, specify `--loss_scale ignore_empty_think` to ignore the loss calculation for `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n`, preventing the loss of reasoning ability. Refer to the training script cite78†here . The custom dataset format is as follows:
L243: 
L244:     {"messages": [
L245:         {"role": "user", "content": "Where is the capital of Zhejiang?"},
L246:         {"role": "assistant", "content": "<think>\n\n</think>\n\n The capital of Zhejiang is Hangzhou."}
L247:     ]}
L248: Option 2: Add `/no_think` to the query in the dataset to avoid the loss of reasoning ability. Refer to the training script cite79†here . The custom dataset format is as follows:
L249: 
L250:     {"messages": [
L251:         {"role": "user", "content": "Where is the capital of Zhejiang? /no_think"},
L252:         {"role": "assistant", "content": "<think>\n\n</think>\n\n The capital of Zhejiang is Hangzhou."}
L253:     ]}
L254: ### 30-Minute Self-Cognition Fine-Tuning
L255: 
L256: This section introduces a 30-minute self-cognition fine-tuning process for the Qwen3-8B model. The required GPU memory is 22GB, and it can be run on the A10 provided by cite80†ModelScope's free compute resources†modelscope.cn .
L257: 
L258: After training, the model will identify itself as "swift-robot," trained by "swift," instead of its original self-cognition as "Qwen," trained by Alibaba Cloud.
L259: If you need to train in an offline environment, you can manually download the model and dataset and specify `--model <model-path>` and `--dataset <dataset-dir>`. The dataset can be found on cite81†Modelscope Hub†modelscope.cn .
L260: For the meaning of each parameter in the training script, please refer to the cite82†Command-line parameters documentation†swift.readthedocs.io .
L261: 
L262:     CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
L263:     swift sft \
L264:         --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
L265:         --train_type lora \
L266:         --dataset 'swift/Qwen3-SFT-Mixin#2000' \
L267:                   'swift/self-cognition:qwen3#600' \
L268:         --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
L269:         --num_train_epochs 1 \
L270:         --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
L271:         --per_device_eval_batch_size 1 \
L272:         --learning_rate 1e-4 \
L273:         --lora_rank 8 \
L274:         --lora_alpha 32 \
L275:         --target_modules all-linear \
L276:         --gradient_accumulation_steps 16 \
L277:         --eval_steps 50 \
L278:         --save_steps 50 \
L279:         --save_total_limit 2 \
L280:         --logging_steps 5 \
L281:         --max_length 2048 \
L282:         --output_dir output \
L283:         --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
L284:         --dataloader_num_workers 4 \
L285:         --model_author swift \
L286:         --model_name swift-robot
L287: After fine-tuning, you can use the following script to test the fine-tuning results. Note that the `--adapters` section needs to be modified to the directory path of the last saved checkpoint:
L288: 
L289:     CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
L290:     swift infer \
L291:         --adapters output/vx-xxx/checkpoint-xxx \
L292:         --stream true \
L293:         --temperature 0 \
L294:         --max_new_tokens 2048
L295: 
L296:     `<<< who are you?
L297:     <think>
L298:     Okay, the user asked, "who are you?" I need to introduce myself. Let me start by stating my name, swift-robot. Then, I should mention that I'm an AI assistant developed by swift. I should explain my purpose, which is to provide information and assistance. I should also highlight my capabilities, like answering questions, generating text, and engaging in conversation. It's important to keep the tone friendly and approachable.
L299: Maybe add something about being here to help and encourage the user to ask anything. Let me check if I covered all the key points: name, developer, purpose, capabilities, and a welcoming statement. Yeah, that should do it. Now, let me put that into a concise and friendly response.
L300:     </think>
L301: 
L302:     Hello! I am swift-robot, an artificial intelligence assistant developed by swift. My purpose is to provide information and assistance to users like you. I can answer questions, generate text, and engage in conversations on a wide range of topics. I am here to help, so feel free to ask me anything you need!
L303:     `
L304: By default, ms-swift will use the ModelScope community to download models and datasets. If you want to use the HuggingFace community, you need to additionally specify `--use_hf true`.
L305: 
L306: Merge LoRA weights:
L307: 
L308:     swift export \
L309:         --adapters output/checkpoint-xxx \
L310:         --merge_lora true
L311: Push the model to ModelScope/HuggingFace:
L312: 
L313:     # If you are pushing the complete weights, you need to change `--adapters` to `--model`.
L314:     # The Modelscope hub_token can be found here: https://modelscope.cn/my/myaccesstoken
L315:     swift export \
L316:         --adapters output/checkpoint-xxx \
L317:         --push_to_hub true \
L318:         --hub_model_id '<hub-model-id>' \
L319:         --hub_token '<hub-token>' \
L320:         --use_hf false
L321: If you want to use multiple GPUs for training, the following provides a demo for multi-GPU training:
L322: 
L323:     # 4 * 60GB
L324:     # You can run the experiment by setting `--dataset AI-ModelScope/alpaca-gpt4-data-en`.
L325:     # Note: If you want to specify `--packing true`, you must additionally set `--attn_impl flash_attn`.
L326: 
L327:     NPROC_PER_NODE=4 \
L328:     CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
L329:     swift sft \
L330:         --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
L331:         --train_type full \
L332:         --dataset '<your-dataset>' \
L333:         --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
L334:         --per_device_train_batch_size 1 \
L335:         --per_device_eval_batch_size 1 \
L336:         --learning_rate 1e-5 \
L337:         --gradient_accumulation_steps 4 \
L338:         --packing true \
L339:         --eval_steps 100 \
L340:         --save_steps 100 \
L341:         --logging_steps 5 \
L342:         --max_length 8192 \
L343:         --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
L344:         --dataloader_num_workers 8 \
L345:         --dataset_num_proc 8 \
L346:         --save_total_limit 2 \
L347:         --save_only_model true \
L348:         --output_dir output \
L349:         --deepspeed zero3 \
L350:         --use_liger_kernel true \
L351:         --attn_impl flash_attn
L352: ## Reinforcement Learning (RL)
L353: 
L354: ms-swift supports RLHF methods such as DPO, GRPO, DAPO, PPO, KTO, and more. This section will focus on an example of using ms-swift to perform GRPO training for Qwen3-8B.
L355: 
L356: For detailed RLHF support information, please refer to: cite83†Supported Features†swift.readthedocs.io .
L357: ### Environment Setup
L358: 
L359: In addition to installing the ms-swift related dependencies introduced above, the following dependencies also need to be installed:
L360: 
L361:     pip install "math_verify==0.5.2"
L362:     pip install vllm
L363: ### Data Preparation
L364: 
L365: The dataset format for GRPO training using ms-swift is similar to that of SFT, except that the assistant part of the last round is not required. If using accuracy as a reward, a `solution` column is needed to calculate the accuracy.
L366: Example Dataset Formats:
L367: 
L368:     {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Tell me tomorrow's weather"}]}
L369:     {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 1 + 1?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "It equals 2"}, {"role": "user", "content": "What about adding 1?"}]}
L370:     {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is your name?"}]}
L371: 
L372: For dataset preparation for other RLHF algorithms, see: cite84†Custom Dataset Documentation†swift.readthedocs.io .
L373: 
L374: Notes on Dataset Requirements:
L375:   * Reward Function Calculation: The dataset format depends on the reward function being used. Additional columns may be required to support specific reward calculations. For instance:
L376:     * When using the built-in accuracy or cosine similarity reward, the dataset must include a `solution` column to calculate the accuracy of the responses.
L377:     * Other columns in the dataset will be passed as `**kwargs` to the reward function for additional customization.
L378:   * Customizing the Reward Function: To adapt the reward function to your specific needs, you can refer to the following resource: cite85†External Reward Plugin . This plugin provides examples and templates for implementing custom reward functions.
L379: During the training process, we use vLLM to accelerate the sampling process. By setting `num_infer_workers=8`, we deploy a vLLM engine for each device to speed up the sampling process.
L380: 
L381:     # 70G*8
L382:     CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
L383:     NPROC_PER_NODE=8 \
L384:     swift rlhf \
L385:         --rlhf_type grpo \
L386:         --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
L387:         --train_type full \
L388:         --dataset 'AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR#5000' \
L389:         --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
L390:         --num_train_epochs 1 \
L391:         --per_device_train_batch_size 2 \
L392:         --per_device_eval_batch_size 2 \
L393:         --learning_rate 1e-6 \
L394:         --save_total_limit 2 \
L395:         --logging_steps 5 \
L396:         --output_dir output \
L397:         --gradient_accumulation_steps 1 \
L398:         --warmup_ratio 0.05 \
L399:         --dataloader_num_workers 4 \
L400:         --max_completion_length 4096 \
L401:         --vllm_max_model_len 8192 \
L402:         --reward_funcs accuracy \
L403:         --num_generations 16 \
L404:         --use_vllm true \
L405:         --vllm_gpu_memory_utilization 0.4 \
L406:         --sleep_level 1 \
L407:         --offload_model true \
L408:         --offload_optimizer true \
L409:         --gc_collect_after_offload true \
L410:         --deepspeed zero3 \
L411:         --num_infer_workers 8 \
L412:         --tensor_parallel_size 1 \
L413:         --temperature 1.0 \
L414:         --top_p 0.85 \
L415:         --log_completions true \
L416:         --overlong_filter true
L417: ## Megatron-SWIFT
L418: 
L419: ms-swift incorporates Megatron parallelism techniques to accelerate the training of large models. The supported models can be found in the cite86†Supported Models Documentation†swift.readthedocs.io .
L420: 
L421: For environment preparation and the conversion between HF and MCore model weights, you can refer to the cite87†Megatron-SWIFT Training Documentation†swift.readthedocs.io . These topics will not be elaborated here.
L422: We will use Alibaba Cloud DLC to start the training The training environment consists of 2 machines with 8 * 80GiB A800 GPUs. For more information on multi-node startup methods, refer to cite88†here .
L423: 
L424:     # https://help.aliyun.com/zh/pai/user-guide/general-environment-variables
L425:     # Ensure that the weight-saving paths on the two nodes are identical.
L426:     NNODES=$WORLD_SIZE \
L427:     NODE_RANK=$RANK \
L428:     megatron sft \
L429:         --load Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base-mcore \
L430:         --dataset 'liucong/Chinese-DeepSeek-R1-Distill-data-110k-SFT' \
L431:         --tensor_model_parallel_size 2 \
L432:         --expert_model_parallel_size 8 \
L433:         --moe_grouped_gemm true \
L434:         --moe_shared_expert_overlap true \
L435:         --moe_aux_loss_coeff 0.01 \
L436:         --micro_batch_size 1 \
L437:         --global_batch_size 16 \
L438:         --packing true \
L439:         --recompute_granularity full \
L440:         --recompute_method uniform \
L441:         --recompute_num_layers 1 \
L442:         --train_iters 2000 \
L443:         --eval_iters 50 \
L444:         --finetune true \
L445:         --cross_entropy_loss_fusion true \
L446:         --lr 1e-5 \
L447:         --lr_warmup_iters 100 \
L448:         --min_lr 1e-6 \
L449:         --save megatron_output/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base \
L450:         --eval_interval 200 \
L451:         --save_interval 200 \
L452:         --max_length 8192 \
L453:         --num_workers 8 \
L454:         --dataset_num_proc 8 \
L455:         --no_save_optim true \
L456:         --no_save_rng true \
